extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering dataset of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, paired with Wikipedia pages and annotated long and short answers when present. It is designed for end-to-end QA research and evaluation.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in Natural Questions were sampled from Google search queries issued by multiple users in a short period of time, and annotators then identified long answers by selecting the smallest HTML bounding box on the corresponding Wikipedia page that contained all information required to answer the question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Both the long and short answer can be NULL if no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page, and the remaining examples without answer labels were not discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Question-Wikipedia page pairs with long-answer bounding boxes and short answers, forming (question, wikipedia page, long answer, short answer) quadruples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Comprehensive guidelines were developed for the task; annotators identified long answers by selecting the smallest HTML bounding box that contains all of the information required to answer the question, and short answers were spans/entities or yes/no answers where applicable. Annotation quality was constantly monitored.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality was evaluated using post hoc correctness judgments of non-null answers under consensus judgments from four experts, and by k-way annotations with k = 25 on a subset of the data.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 25-way annotations on a subset of the data; consensus judgments from four experts for post hoc evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may reflect biases from using Wikipedia as the evidence source and from the selection of real Google search queries; the authors note that "like any data set there may be biases in this choice."
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are limited to longer queries (8+ words) that pass heuristic filters and have a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results, so the dataset may not generalize to shorter queries, "how to" questions, or non-Wikipedia domains. The task also includes many unanswerable examples and answers can be ambiguous or variable across annotators.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the benchmark as useful for advancing natural language understanding and question answering systems that have "significant utility to users."
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Anonymized aggregated Google search queries are used as questions; no explicit sensitive human attributes are described as being collected.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for QA research, including large-scale end-to-end training data, development/evaluation, and baseline benchmarking. The public release includes training, development, and sequestered test splits.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was filtered and sampled from Google search queries: only queries of 8 words or more were kept, and a subset was selected using heuristic patterns; queries without a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered using heuristics to remove non-questions, and annotators selected the smallest HTML bounding box on the Wikipedia page containing enough information to answer the question; pages were limited to Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
